newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SINGAPORE GOVERNMENT SECURITIES END NARROWLY MIXED.
newsitem.headline: SINGAPORE GOVERNMENT SECURITIES END NARROWLY MIXED.

text.p: Singapore government securities ended narrowly mixed in moderate trade on Wednesday on retail and interbank interest, dealers said.

"Government securities ended narrowly mixed today despite a small hike in the interbank rate. Treasury bill yields were slightly higher but bond prices were slightly lower. Volume was moderate," a local dealer said.
In treasury bills, three-months closed at a yield of 2.06/2.01 percent compared with Tuesday's yield of 2.00/1.95 percent and one-year at a yield of 2.30/2.25 percent against 2.27/2.22 percent.
Among bonds, April 1999 ended at S$98.85/98.90 from Tuesday's close of S$98.95/99.00, May 2002 at S$99.78/99.83 versus S$99.88/99.93 and June 2003 at S$94.90/94.95 against S$94.95/95.00.
The overnight interbank offered rate rose to 1-11/16 1-9/16 percent from Tuesday's 1-5/8 1-1/2 percent.
